parole.testo: Borrowed into Turkish dialects from dialectal forms of Greek φάλαινα (fálaina), from Ancient Greek φάλλαινα (phállaina, “whale”). Doublet of balina (“whale”).
Borrowed from Greek [Term?].
From Ottoman Turkish [script needed] (aftos), Greek αυτός (aftós, “this one (masculine singular demonstrative)”); the sense development is unclear.
From Greek αυτός ποιος (είναι;) (aftós poios (eínai;), “who (is) this one?”, a pejorative expression). Compare Turkish kıtıpiyos.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آختاپود (ahtapot), from Greek οχταπόδι (ochtapódi).

parole.significato: whirlpool, eddy, vortex, swirl, a body of rotating water produced by opposing currents
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آنافور (anafor, “whirlpool, eddy”), from Greek αναφορά (anaforá, “reference, report, account”), ultimately from Ancient Greek ἀναφορά (anaphorá, “reference”).
From Ottoman Turkish آناختار (anahtar), from Greek ανοιχτήρι (anoichtíri).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آنغاریه (angarya, angariya, angariye), from Greek αγγαρεία (angareía).

parole.significato: seam, a joint between the planks of a wooden ship or boat
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آرموز (armuz, armoz, “seam in a wooden boat”), from Greek αρμός (armós, “joint, union; seam”), ultimately from Ancient Greek ἁρμός (harmós, “joint”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آترینه (aterine, aterina, “sandsmelt”), from Greek αθερίνα (atherína, “smelt”), ultimately from Ancient Greek ἀθερίνη (atherínē, “smelt”).

parole.significato: mugwort, any flowering plant of the species Artemisia vulgaris, traditionally used medicinally
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آیواطنه (ayvadana, “mugwort”), from Greek αγριοβότανο (agriovótano), a compound of άγριος (ágrios, “wild, uncultivated”) and βότανο (vótano, “herb”).
From Ottoman Turkish آغستوس (ağustos), from Greek Αύγουστος (Ávgoustos), from Latin Latin Augustus
From Ottoman Turkish بابافنغو (babafingo), from Greek παπαφίγκος (papafígkos), from Venetan papafìgo (modern Italian pappafico).
From Greek παχνί (pachní) or an Anatolian Greek cognate, from Ancient Greek φάτνη (phátnē).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish واریوس (varyos), which derives from Greek βαρειός (vareiós).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish باربونیه (barbunya, “the red mullet, mullus barbatus”), from Greek μπαρμπούνια (barmpoúnia), plural of μπαρμπούνι (barmpoúni, “striped red mullet”).
From Ottoman Turkish ببر (biber), from Greek πιπέρι, πιπεριά (pipéri, piperiá).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جنبس (cımbıs), itself from Greek τσιμπίδι (tsimpídi).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish دفنه, from Greek δάφνη (dáfni). Doublet of taflan.

parole.significato: bundle, bunch, wisp, a group of objects held together by wrapping or tying
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish دمت (demet, “bundle, bunch; sheaf, faggot”), from Greek δεμάτι (demáti, “bale, sheaf”), from the mediaeval Byzantine Greek δεμάτιν (demátin), from Koine Greek δεμάτιον (demátion), diminutive of δέμα (déma, “band”).
Borrowed into Turkish dialects from dialectal forms of Greek δελφίνι (delfíni), from Ancient Greek δελφίς (delphís, “dolphin”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طوماتس (domates).
From Ottoman Turkish [script needed] (drahmi), from Greek δραχμή (drachmí), from Ancient Greek δραχμή (drakhmḗ). Doublet of dirhem and drahoma.

parole.significato: property or payment given by a wife to a husband at the time of marriage, dowry.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish [script needed] (drahoma), from Greek τράχωμα (tráchoma, “dowry given in money”), from Byzantine Greek τραχύ (trakhú, “trachy, a kind of Byzantine silver coin”, literally “rough, eneven”), neuter of τραχύς (trakhús, “rough, eneven”), referring to the concavity of the coins.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طغان (tığan), from Greek τηγάνι (tigáni).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish افندی (efendi), from Greek αφέντης (aféntis), from Ancient Greek αὐθέντης (authéntēs). Doublet of otantik.
Derived from Greek Αιγαίο (Aigaío, “Aegean”), from Ancient Greek Αἰγαῖον (Aigaîon).
From Greek άξων (áxon).
Borrowed from Greek εντάξει (entáxei).

parole.significato: viper, adder, any venomous snake in the family Viperidae, but especially the common European adder (Vipera berus)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish انكرك (engerek, “adder”), from Greek εγχελάκι (encheláki), itself a diminutive of Ancient Greek ἔγχελυς (énkhelus, “eel”).
Borrowed from Greek καραβίδα (karavída), perhaps influenced by dialectal engeç (standard Turkish yengeç (“crab”))

parole.significato: artichoke, a plant with enlarged flower heads eaten as a vegetable while immature (Cynara cardunculus var. scolymus)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish انكنار (inginar, enginar, “artichoke”) from Greek αγκινάρα (agkinára, “artichoke”) from Byzantine Greek ἀγκινάρα (ankinára) from Ancient Greek κινάρα (kinára).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فانتی (fanti), from Greek φάντης (fántis, “jack”), from Italian fante (“infantryman; knave, jack”).
Borrowed from Greek φασαρία (fasaría, “unwanted noise”) from Italian fesseria (“stupidity, nonsense”).

parole.significato: bean, any herbaceous plant of the genus Phaseolus and the edible seed of such a plant
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فاصولیه (fasulye, fasulya), from Greek φασολιά (fasoliá).

parole.significato: pennyroyal, pudding grass, a plant of the species Mentha pulegium, used in various medicinal treatments
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فلسكون (filiskün, filiskin), from Greek φλησκούνι (fliskoúni, “pennyroyal”).
From Ottoman Turkish فلز (filiz, “shoot, tendril, young plant”), from early modern Greek φυλλίς (fyllís), from Ancient Greek φῠ́λλον (phŭ́llon, “leaf”).
Borrowed from Greek Φύρα (Fýra).

parole.significato: the amount you can carry between two fingertips that touch each other
parole.testo: Borrowed from Greek φούσκα (foúska, “blister”) from Ancient Greek φυσάω (phusáō, “to blow”).

parole.significato: vetch, any of several leguminous plants of the genus Vicia, specifically the common vetch (Vicia sativa)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فیك (fiğ, “vetch”), from Greek βικίον (vikíon), ultimately from Latin vicia (“vetch”).

parole.significato: greenfinch, any bird within the genus Chloris, specifically Chloris chloris
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فلوریه (florya), from Greek φλώρια (flória), plural form of φλώρι (flóri), variant of χλώρι (chlóri, “greenfinch”).

parole.significato: nest egg, an egg or egg-shaped object placed at a spot for a hen to lay her eggs there
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فول (fol, “a nest-egg”), from Greek φώλι (fóli, “the act or place of incubation, nest”), from Ancient Greek φωλεός (phōleós, “den, animal burrow”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فوللق (folluk), from Greek φώλι (fóli, “nest egg”). Equivalent to fol + -luk.
From Ottoman Turkish فوسفور, ultimately from Greek φωσφόρος (fosfóros, “light bearing”).
From Ottoman Turkish فونده (funda), from Greek φούντα (foúnta, “shrub; flake, fringe”) from Hellenistic φοῦνδα (phoûnda), from Latin funda (“hand-sling, net”).

parole.significato: a dragnet or dredge used for sponge fishing
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish غانگاوه (gangava), from Greek γαγγάβα (gangáva), from Ancient Greek γαγγάμη (gangámē), variant of γάγγαμον (gángamon, “small net for oystercatching”).
Borrowed from Greek κατσαβίδι (katsavídi).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كم (gem, “bit”), from Greek κημός (kimós, “muzzle; nosebag”).
Borrowed from Greek κολίανδρο (kolíandro, “coriander”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كونیه, from Greek γωνία (gonía, “corner”). Compare Classical Syriac ܓܘܢܝܐ, Persian گونیا.
From Ottoman Turkish خمسی (hamsı), from Greek χαμψί (champsí), possibly from an ancient Black Sea substrate.
From Ottoman Turkish خانی (hani, “big red fish”), from Greek χάννη (chánni, “serranus hepatus”).

parole.significato: halloumi (a traditional cheese from Cyprus, made from goat's and/or sheep's milk)
parole.testo: Derived from Greek χαλλούμιν (challoúmin), from Egyptian Arabic حلوم (ḥalūm) or North Levantine Arabic حلوم, from Arabic حلم (ḥilm).

parole.significato: stake or pole used to support grapevines or other climbing plants
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish هرك (herek, “stake, pole”), from Greek χαράκιον (charákion), diminutive of Ancient Greek χάραξ (khárax, “pole, vine prop, pointed stake”).

parole.significato: Christian (pertaining to Jesus Christ, Christianity, or Christians)
parole.testo: From Greek Χριστιανός (Christianós).
From Ottoman Turkish خونی (huni), from Greek χουνί (chouní), χωνί (choní, “funnel”), from Ancient Greek χῶνος (khônos), χώνη (khṓnē), contracted of χοάνη (khoánē, “funnel”).
From Ottoman Turkish اسقامبیل (iskambil) from Greek σκαμπίλι (skampíli, “card game”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اسكمله (iskemle), from Greek σκαμνί (skamní), ultimately from Latin scamnum.
From Ottoman Turkish اسقورپیت (iskorpit), borrowed from Greek σκορπίδι (skorpídi).

parole.significato: finch, any passerine bird of the family Fringillidae, especially the chaffinch (Fringilla coelebs)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اسپنوز (ispinoz, “finch”), from Greek σπίνος (spínos, “finch”), ultimately from Ancient Greek σπῐ́νος (spĭ́nos, “chaffinch”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish استاوریت (istavrit), استاورید (istavrid), from Greek σταυρίδι (stavrídi), σαυρίδι (savrídi), from Byzantine Greek σαυρίδιον (saurídion), diminutive of σαυρίς (saurís) (classically σαῦρος (saûros)).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish استاوروز (istavroz), from Greek σταυρός (stavrós).
From Ottoman Turkish استریدیه, from Greek στρείδι (streídi, “cockle”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قلمار (kalamar), from Greek καλαμάρι (kalamári). Doublet of kalem.

parole.significato: dotterel, any small brown-and-black bird of the species Charadrius morinellus
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قالینیس (kalinis, “dotterel”), from Greek [script needed] (galinis).

parole.significato: pin, a small nail with a head and a sharp point
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قارفیچه (karfiçe), from Greek καρφίτσα (karfítsa, “pin”), itself a diminutive of καρφί (karfí, “nail”).
From Greek καρίδες (karídes).

parole.significato: kind of bowl-shaped vessel carved from a single piece of wood
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قاوطه (kavata, “wooden bowl”), from Greek καβάθα (kavátha), from Byzantine Greek γαβάθα (gabátha), ultimately from Latin gabata (“kind of dish or platter”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كفال (kefal), from Greek κέφαλος (kéfalos).
From Greek καλαθαριά f (kalathariá), καλάθια f (kaláthia), καλάθι n (kaláthi, “basket”)

parole.significato: hemp, cannabis, any tall, annual herb of the species Cannabis sativa, native to Asia
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كنویر (kenevir), from Greek κανναβούρι (kannavoúri, “hempseed”), a derivative of καννάβι (kannávi, “hemp”), ultimately from Ancient Greek κάννᾰβῐς (kánnăbĭs, “hemp”).
From Ottoman Turkish كراتا (kerata), from كراته (kerata), borrowed from Greek κερατάς (keratás, “cornuto”).
From Ottoman Turkish كروت (kerevet), from Greek κρεβάτι (kreváti), from Ancient Greek κράββατος (krábbatos).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كروت (kerevit, “crayfish”), from Greek καραβίδα (karavída).
From Greek καρτάριζω (kartárizo).

parole.significato: ballan wrasse, any marine fish of the species Labrus bergylta, found in the Atlantic Ocean
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish [Term?], from Greek κίχλη (kíchli, “thrush”), ultimately from Ancient Greek κῐ́χλη (kĭ́khlē, “thrush; wrasse”).

parole.significato: cherry, any tree or shrub of the species Prunus subg. Cerasus and its small, edible fruit
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كراز (kiraz, “cherry”), from Greek κεράσι (kerási, “cherry”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كرن (kiren), كورن (güren), from Greek κράνο (kráno).

Borrowed from Greek κοχλίας (kochlías, “snail”), with the ending -angoz from synonymous salyangoz (“snail”). Compare Middle Armenian կոխլանճ (koxlanč), Armenian կողինջ (koġinǰ), which underwent a similar contamination. Possibly phonetically influenced by koklanmak (“to be smelled”).
From Greek κοχλίας (kochlías).
From Ottoman Turkish قوقورج, from Greek κοκορέτσι (kokorétsi), from Albanian kukurec.

parole.significato: chub mackerel, either of two scombroid fish of the species Scomber colias and Scomber japonicus
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قولیوز (kolyoz), from Greek κολιός (koliós), ultimately from Ancient Greek κολῐ́ᾱς (kolĭ́ās, “chub mackerel”).
From Ottoman Turkish قوقله, from Greek κούκλα (koúkla, “doll”).
From Ottoman Turkish قوقوماو (kukumav), borrowed from Greek κουκουβάγια (koukouvágia, “owl”).

parole.significato: bogue, any fish of the species Boops boops, native to the eastern Atlantic
parole.testo: From Greek γόπες (gópes), plural of γόπα (gópa, “bogue”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قوطی (kutu, kutı), from Greek κουτί (koutí).
Compound of köpek (“dog”) + balık (“fish”), likely a calque of Greek σκυλόψαρο (skylópsaro).

parole.significato: kind of porous limestone containing noticeable quantities of fossils or seashells, used as a construction material
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كوفكی (küfeki), from Greek κουφάκι (koufáki, “pumice stone”).

From Ottoman Turkish قتیپیوس (kıtıpiyos), from a dialectal form of Greek και αυτός ποιος (είναι;) (kai aftós poios (eínai;), “and who (is) this one?”, a pejorative expression for a worthless person). Compare Turkish aftospiyos.

parole.significato: East Atlantic peacock wrasse, any wrasse of the species Symphodus tinca, living in shallow waters and rocky shores
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لاپینه (lapina), from Greek λάμπαινα (lámpaina, “wrasse”).
Borrowed from Greek λέπρα (lépra), from Ancient Greek λέπρα (lépra, “leprosy”).
From Ottoman Turkish لورك, from Greek λαβράκι (lavráki).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لیپسوس (lipsos, “red scorpionfish”), itself from Greek λειψός (leipsós), from Ancient Greek λείπω (leípō, “to leave behind, remain”).

From Ottoman Turkish لوفر, from Greek λουφάρι (loufári), a form of γουφάρι n (goufári), γοφάρι (gofári), from Byzantine Greek γο(υ)μφάριον (go(u)mphárion), from Hellenistic Koine Greek γόμφος (gómphos) + ending -άριον (-árion).

parole.significato: conger eel, any of various large marine eels of the genus Conger
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish میغره (mığra, “conger eel”), from Greek μουγγρί (moungrí).
Perhaps from Greek μαλάκας (malákas).
From Ottoman Turkish مناستر (manastır), from Greek μοναστήρι (monastíri), from Koine Greek μοναστήριον (monastḗrion).
From Ottoman Turkish مانطار (mantar), from Greek μανιτάρι (manitári).
From Ottoman Turkish ماستیقه, ماستیقا (mastika), from Greek μαστίχα (mastícha), from Ancient Greek μαστίχη (mastíkhē). Doublet of mezdeke.
From Greek μέθυσος (méthysos).
From Ottoman Turkish مایس (mayıs), from Greek Μάιος (Máios), from Latin Maius.
From Ottoman Turkish ماچه (maça), from Greek μάτσα (mátsa) and Sicilian mazzi (cognate to Italian mazzi m pl).
Borrowed from Greek μέλισσα (mélissa). Doublet of melisa.

parole.significato: breakwater, jetty, mole, a construction in or around a harbour designed to break the force of the sea
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مندرك (mendirek), from Greek μανδράκι (mandráki), diminutive of μάνδρα (mándra, “fold, pen, barn”).
Borrowed from Greek με το ζόρι (me to zóri, “by force”), itself derived from Ottoman Turkish زور (zor).

parole.significato: mussel, any edible, saltwater mollusc of the order Mytilida, especially the ones in the genus Mytilus
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مدیه (midya, “mussel”), from Greek μύδια (mýdia), plural of μύδι (mýdi, “mussel”), from Ancient Greek μύδιον (múdion), the diminutive of μῦς (mûs, “mouse; mussel”).
Borrowed from Greek μόλος (mólos, “jetty; molee”).

parole.significato: cod, any sea fish of the genus Gadus, especially the Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مورینه (morina, “cod”), from Greek μουρούνα (mouroúna).

parole.significato: linen closet, a shelved closet used for the storage of bedlinen and associated bedding
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish موصندره (musandıra), from the unattested Greek word *μεσάνδηρο (*mesándiro, “pedestal, mezzanine, balcony”).
From Ottoman Turkish مشمله (muşmula), from Greek μούσμουλο (moúsmoulo).

parole.significato: the act of leaving land fallowed (ploughed but left unseeded)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish نطاس (nadas), from Greek νεατός (neatós), ultimately from Ancient Greek νέος (néos, “new”).

parole.significato: little darling, sweet thing (term of endearment)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Greek νονός (nonós, “godfather”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوركینوس (orkinos), from Greek όρκινος (órkinos), from Ancient Greek ὄρκῡνος (órkūnos), variant of ὄρκῡς (órkūs, “large kind of tunny”).

parole.significato: pinking, any kind of needlework or embroidery with scalloped edges made as a border or insertion
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اویا (oya, “pinking”), from Greek ούγια (oúgia, “sheepskin; fringe, edge”), ultimately from Ancient Greek ᾤα (ōía, “sheepskin; border, fringe of a garment”).

parole.significato: acorn, the fruit of the oak, being an oval nut growing in a woody cup or cupule
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پالاموت (palamut, “acorn”), from Greek βαλανίδιον (valanídion, “acorn”), from Ancient Greek βάλανος (bálanos, “acorn”).
Borrowed from Greek παλιατζούρα (paliatzoúra)
From Ottoman Turkish پالیقاریا (palikarya), from Greek παλικάρια (palikária), plural of παλικάρι (palikári).
From Ottoman Turkish پانایر (panayir), from Greek πανηγύρι (panigýri, “gathering of people”) from Ancient Greek πανήγυρις (panḗguris, “high festival”).
From Ottoman Turkish پاپاز (papaz), from Greek παπάς (papás, “priest”).

From Ottoman Turkish پاسقالیه (paskalya), borrowed from Greek Πασχαλιά (Paschaliá, “Eastertide”), from Byzantine Greek Πασχαλία (Paskhalía), from Koine Greek πασχάλιος (paskhálios, adjective) in the phrase πασχαλία γιορτή (paskhalía giortḗ, “Easter feast”), from Koine Greek πάσχα (páskha, “Passover”
Borrowed from Greek πάστρα (pástra), from Greek παστρεύω (pastrévo).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پاتاتس (patates), from Greek πατάτες (patátes), from Spanish patata, from Taíno batata.

parole.significato: a small slipper, baby shoe, knitted sock
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish پاتیك (patik), in turn borrowed from Greek πατήκι (patíki), πατίκι (patíki, “slipper”), from πατώ (pató, “to tread”) + -ίκι (-íki).

parole.significato: edible crab, brown crab, any kind of robust crab of the species Cancer pagurus
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پاغوریه (pağurya, “kind of crab”), from Greek πάγουρος (págouros, “hermit crab”), ultimately from Ancient Greek πᾰ́γουρος (pắgouros, “crab”)
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پاچاوره (paçavra), from Greek πατσαβούρα (patsavoúra, “rag; dirty cloth”).
Maybe from Greek, but the term is uncertain.
From Ottoman Turkish بكسمات (peksimet), بكسماد (beksemad), from Greek παξιμάδι (paximádi, “twice-baked piece of bread”).

parole.significato: A dish of (usually) beans or seafood, cooked in a savoury sauce of tomato paste, chopped onions, garlic and typically c…
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish پلكی (plaki, pilaki), from Greek πλακί (plakí).
From Ottoman Turkish پسقپوس, from Greek επίσκοπος (epískopos).

parole.significato: hub, nave, the central part, usually cylindrical, of a wheel
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پویرا (poyra, “nave, hub of the wheel”), from Greek πορεία (poreía, “course, track, direction of movement”).
From Ottoman Turkish پویراز (poyraz), from Old Anatolian Turkish فوریاز (foryāz), پوریاز (poryaz), from Greek βοριάς (voriás). Compare Gagauz poyraz.
From Greek [Term?].

parole.significato: leek, any vegetable with edible leaves of the species Allium ampeloprasum
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پراصه (pırasa, prasa), from Greek πράσα (prása), plural of πράσο (práso, “leek”), itself from Ancient Greek πράσον (práson, “leek”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish رادیكیه (radikiye), from Greek ραδίκια (radíkia), plural form of ραδίκι (radíki, “chicory”), ultimately from Italian radicchio.
From Ottoman Turkish روقه (roka), from Greek ρόκα (róka). Whereas اروقه (aruka) is from Italian eruca. All from Latin ērūca (“rocket”).
From Ottoman Turkish صلیانقوس (“snail”), from Greek σάλιαγγας (sáliangas).
From Ottoman Turkish صالچه (salça, “sauce, gravy”), from Greek σάλτσα (sáltsa), from Italian salsa. Doublet of sos and salsa, from Vulgar Latin.
From Greek σαρδέλα (sardéla).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سمر (semer, “packsaddle”), from Greek σαμάρι (samári, “packsaddle”), diminutive of Ancient Greek σάγμα (ságma, “packsaddle”).
From Greek συναγωγή (synagogí).

parole.significato: butt, the joint where two planks in a strake meet
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish صوقره (sokra, “butt”), from Greek σώχορο (sóchoro, “filling piece”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish صویا (soya, “penknife, clasp-knife”), from Greek σουγιάς (sougiás, “penknife, pocketknife”).

parole.significato: razor clam, razor shell, any clam in the genus Solen, with long shells resembling razors
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سولنه (sulina, sulna, “razor clam”), from Greek σωλήνας (solínas, “pipe, tube, duct”), from the accusative plural of Ancient Greek σωλήν (sōlḗn, “channel, pipe”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish صره, صیرا (sıra), from Greek σειρά (seirá).
Compound of tahta and Greek κοριός (koriós, “bug, bedbug”) reanalyzed as kuru.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طاقوز (takoz), ultimately from Greek τάκος (tákos, “chock, wedge”).
Borrowed from Greek τακούνι (takoúni, “heel of shoe”).

parole.significato: storm, cyclone, hurricane, especially a humid one
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طالاز (talaz), from Old Anatolian Turkish طلز (talaz), from Greek θάλασσα (thálassa).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تكیر, from Greek τίγρη (tígri). Cognate with English tiger.
From Ottoman Turkish تمل (temel), from Greek θεμέλιο (themélio, “foundation, base”), from Ancient Greek θεμέλιος (themélios, “belonging to the foundation”).

parole.significato: typhoid fever, abdominal typhus, a disease by the a bacterium of the subspecies Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish توفو (tifo), from Greek τύφος (týfos). Doublet of tifüs (“typhus”).

parole.significato: clover, trefoil, any plant of the genus Trifolium, with leaves usually divided into three (rarely four) leaflets
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طرفیل (tırfıl, “clover”), from Greek τριφύλλι (trifýlli, “clover, trefoil”).

parole.significato: larger type of bonito found in the Black Sea, Marmara Sea, Mediterranean Sea and Atlantic Ocean
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طوریق (torık, toruk), from Greek ταρίχιον (taríchion), diminutive form of Ancient Greek τᾰ́ρῑχος (tắrīkhos, “smoked fish”).
From Ottoman Turkish طوغله (tuğla), توغله (tuğla), from Greek τούγλα (toúgla, “roof cover made of terracotta, tile”), from Latin tēgula (“a tile”), related to tegō (“to cover”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طرپان (tırpan, “scythe”), from Greek δρεπάνι (drepáni).

parole.significato: mackerel, any edible fish of the species Scomber scombrus
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اسقومری (uskumru, “mackerel”), from Greek σκουμπρί (skoumprí, “mackerel”), from Ancient Greek σκομβρίς (skombrís), diminutive of σκόμβρος (skómbros, “mackerel”).

parole.significato: fender, any cushion-like object, made of rubber, wood, or fibres of old rope, that is placed along the sides of a boat…
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوستورماچه (usturmaça, “fender”), from Greek στρομάτσα (stromátsa), variant of στρομάτσο (stromátso, “fender”), from Italian stramazzo (“straw mattress, pallet”), perhaps under the influence of στρώμα (stróma, “mattress”).
From Ottoman Turkish وافتیس (vaftis), وافتیز (vaftiz), from Greek βάφτισμα (váftisma).

parole.significato: ray, skate, any of various marine fish in the superorder Batoidea, especially the thornback ray (Raja clavata)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish واطوس (vatos, “ray, skate”), from Greek βάτος (vátos, “skate”), from Ancient Greek βάτος (bátos, “kind of skate”).
From Ottoman Turkish ورنیك (vernik), itself from Greek βερνίκη (verníki) or Italian vernice.
From Ottoman Turkish ویده (vida), (via Greek) from Venetan vida.

parole.significato: the smaller version of several scombroid fish, such as the mackerel or the sardine, generally measuring between 12 and…
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ونوس (vonos), from Greek βόνος (vónos, “small mackerel or bonito”).

parole.significato: phosphorescence in the sea due to bioluminescent dinoflagellates
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish یقاموز, یاقاموز (yakamoz), from Greek διακαμός (diakamós).
From Ottoman Turkish یالی (yalı), from Greek γιαλός (gialós, “beach”).
From Ottoman Turkish یورتی (yortu), from Greek γιορτή (giortí), from Ancient Greek ἑορτή (heortḗ).

parole.significato: needlefish, garfish, any long and slender fish of the species Belone belone
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زارغنه (zargana), from Greek ζαργάνα (zargána, “needlefish”).
From Greek ζοφερός (zoferós), from Ancient Greek ζόφος (zóphos).

parole.significato: sinker, a weight used in fishing to cause the line or net to sink
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زوقه (zoka, “fishhook”), from Greek ζόκα (zóka, “fishhook”), from Venetan soga (“rope”), ultimately from Late Latin sōca (“rope”), from Gaulish *soucā.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زوراكی (zoraki), from Greek ζοράκι (zoráki), derived from Greek ζόρι (zóri) and -άκι (-áki). Etymologically related to Turkish zor. Compare Azerbaijani zorakı, Persian زورکی, borrowings from Ottoman Turkish.

parole.significato: crazy – used only in the fixed phrase zırdeli, added as an intensifier to deli (crazy)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Greek ζουρλός (zourlós, “crazy”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چوپره (çupra), from Greek τσιπούρα (tsipoúra).
Borrowed from Greek τσίρος (tsíros, “swordfish”).

parole.significato: distaff, rock, a device to which a bundle of fibres are attached for temporary storage, before being spun
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوركه (öreke, “distaff”), from Greek ρόκα (róka, “distaff”), ultimately from Italian rocca (“distaff”).

parole.significato: oakum, tow, an untwisted bundle of fibres used to seal gaps
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish استوپی (üstüpü, “oakum, tow”), itself from Greek στουπί (stoupí).

parole.significato: goad, prod, any long, pointed stick used to spur or guide livestock
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوكندره (üğendire, üvendire, “goad”), from Greek βουκέντρα (voukéntra, “goad, prod”).

parole.significato: rowan, service tree, any of various small, deciduous trees or bushes of the genus Sorbus
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوز (üvez, “rowan, service tree”), from Greek [script needed] (uves), ultimately from Ancient Greek ὄᾱ (óā, “service tree”).
From Ottoman Turkish اسقره (ıskara), from Greek σχάρα (schára).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ایغرب (ığrıb), from Greek γρίπος (grípos).

parole.significato: former name of the Karaköy neighborhood in Istanbul
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish غلطه, either borrowed from Greek Γαλατία (Galatía, “Galatia”) from Ancient Greek Γᾰλᾰ́τᾱς (Gălắtās, “Galatian”) or from Greek γαλατάς (galatás, “milkman”).

parole.significato: stowage, stacking, piling, the act or practice of placing items neatly on top of each other
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish استیف (istif, “stowage, stacking”), from either Greek στοίβα (stoíva, “pile of, stack of”) or Italian stivare (“to stow, to load”).

parole.significato: A brownish purple or blue area on skin; a bruise, contusion.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish مورارمق (morarmaḳ, “to become purple”), from Ottoman Turkish مور (mor, “a violet color or dye, violet, purple”), either borrowed from Greek μούρο (moúro, “mulberry”), from Ancient Greek μόρον (móron, “black mulberry, blackberry”) or from Armenian մոռ (moṙ, “blackberry”), morphol
Descended from Ottoman Turkish پالاوره (palavra), from either Greek παλάβρα (palávra) or Ladino palavra, ultimately from Old Spanish palabra.
